name: Planning Poker
highLevelGoals: The moderator aims to easily set up new Planning Poker games, define items for estimation, and invite participants to ensure a smooth start to the sprint goal setting process.
The moderator seeks to modify, add, or remove items from the estimation list dynamically to reflect the team's evolving understanding and priorities during a session.
The moderator wants to control the flow of estimation, including selecting items, revealing estimates, and accepting final estimates, to drive productive discussions and reach consensus.
The moderator desires methods to quickly import or copy/paste multiple stories into the game, reducing manual effort and accelerating game setup.
The moderator needs to review past game sessions, including stories and their estimates, and export this data for record-keeping or further analysis.
The moderator expects to create, log in to, modify, and delete their account details, including password recovery, to maintain control over their application access and data.
The moderator aims to configure estimation scales and manage the number of participants to tailor the game environment to their team's specific agile practices.
The estimator wants to join games, view the current story being estimated, and submit their estimates effectively to contribute to sprint goal setting.
The estimator needs to see all items planned for estimation in a session and view prior estimates for the current story to inform their decision-making.
The participant desires visibility into who has estimated and the ability to initiate a timer to manage discussion time, fostering productive team conversations.
The participant expects a consistent display of estimation cards and personalized elements like thumbnail photos to enhance the user experience and clarity.
The developer aims to build an application that adheres to web standards (XHTML, CSS), functions across major browsers, and complies with W3C accessibility guidelines to maximize user reach.
The developer seeks to implement database indexing and efficient coding practices to ensure fast response times and reliable data handling.
The user expects the application to react quickly to their inputs, display information clearly, and provide helpful feedback through well-designed error pages.
The user requires the ability to use Unicode characters within the application to accommodate various languages and special characters.
The researcher aims to access game results stored in a non-identifiable format to conduct studies on estimation patterns and team dynamics without compromising privacy.
lowLevelGoals: The moderator can initiate a new game session, providing a name or identifier for the game.
The moderator can input or select multiple stories or tasks that need to be estimated in the current game session.
The moderator can send invitations (e.g., via a link or email) to other users to join the active Planning Poker game.
The moderator can edit the description, title, or any other relevant attribute of a story or task already added to the estimation list.
The moderator can append a new story or task to the list of items pending estimation during an active game session.
The moderator can delete a story or task from the list of items to be estimated in the ongoing game session.
The moderator can designate which story or task is currently being estimated by the participants.
The moderator can trigger the display of all individual estimates submitted by participants for the currently selected story.
The moderator can confirm and record a chosen estimate (e.g., the average, a specific participant's estimate) as the final estimate for the current story.
The moderator can upload a file (e.g., CSV, JSON) containing a list of stories or tasks to be added to the game.
The moderator can copy text containing multiple stories or tasks and paste them directly into the application to create new estimation items.
The moderator can view a history of all previously conducted Planning Poker games they have managed.
The moderator can select a past game and see all the stories estimated in that session, along with their final accepted estimates.
The moderator can download the data from past game sessions (e.g., stories, estimates, participants) in a structured format (e.g., CSV, JSON).
The moderator can register for a new account by providing necessary credentials (e.g., email, password).
The moderator can authenticate themselves to access the application using their registered credentials.
The moderator can update personal information associated with their account (e.g., name, email, profile picture).
The moderator can update their password for security reasons.
The moderator can initiate a password reset process (e.g., via email verification) if they forget their login credentials.
The moderator can permanently remove their account and associated data from the application.
The moderator can select or define the set of numerical values (e.g., Fibonacci sequence, T-shirt sizes) that participants can use for estimation.
The moderator can define a limit on how many individuals can join a specific Planning Poker session.
The estimator can enter a game session, typically using an invitation link or game ID provided by the moderator.
The estimator can see the details (e.g., title, description) of the story or task that the moderator has selected for the current estimation round.
The estimator can select a value from the defined estimation scale and submit it as their estimate for the active story.
The estimator can access a list of all stories or tasks that are part of the current game session, including those not yet estimated.
If a story is being re-estimated, the estimator can see their previously submitted estimate for that specific story.
The participant can view indicators (e.g., checkmarks, darkened avatars) next to other participants' names, showing who has already submitted their estimate for the current story.
The participant can start a countdown timer to manage the duration of discussions for a specific story.
The participant observes that the visual representation of estimation values (e.g., card design, font) remains uniform throughout the application.
The participant can see their uploaded profile picture or avatar displayed within the game interface.
The developer implements the front-end code to comply with XHTML markup language specifications.
The developer implements the styling of the application to comply with CSS specifications.
The developer tests and optimizes the application to work correctly and consistently on popular browsers like Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge.
The developer implements features and design choices that meet W3C's Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) to make the application usable for people with disabilities.
The developer configures appropriate indexes on database tables to optimize query performance and reduce response times.
The developer writes code that is optimized for performance, resource usage, and maintainability, following best practices and design patterns.
The developer implements robust error handling, data validation, and transaction management to prevent data corruption and ensure consistency.
The user observes that the application processes their clicks, keystrokes, and other interactions with minimal delay.
The user finds that text, images, and other content within the application are legible, well-organized, and easy to understand.
When an error occurs, the user is presented with clear, informative error messages and guidance on how to resolve the issue or what happened.
The user can type and view text containing characters from various languages and special symbols without corruption or display issues.
The researcher can retrieve data from completed game sessions where all personally identifiable information of participants has been anonymized or removed.
